name: Effective Range / Proper Ordered Sample Compression
proof: Fix an order of the class, retain every active-coordinate example, and decode to the least class member consistent with it. The decoder is proper and remains consistent with the full sample because inactive coordinates have a common label. This proper order-compression scheme retains at most \(\mathrm E(\mathcal H)\) examples.
witness_verification: For #classes/halfintervals with n>=4, the established endpoint values or bounds, in parameter order, are $n-1$ and $1$. The first parameter divided by one plus the second tends to infinity. Thus no reverse affine-linear bound holds. See the database-owned endpoint value proofs.
